BLOCKER: Required tests are absent: no test proves tenant isolation survives the restore round-trip, none proves retention (AURE) does not block the insert slow path, and the integration suite asserts no PostgreSQL 16 requirement (AC explicitly demands all three).

EDP service startup coverage check and the ops cron wiring (emitting `audit_partition_months_ahead` / `audit_partition_low_coverage_total` + stale-job alert) do not exist anywhere in the diff; the AC is unimplemented outside the two CLIs.

`pfaudit Down` takes no advisory lock or ACCESS EXCLUSIVE: concurrent app inserts during the down window land in the (renamed) shadow and become invisible to readers of the flat `audit` — silent data loss on the emergency rollback path.

0014 §17 runs `SELECT min(at) FROM audit` with no `to_regclass('audit')` guard: on any database where the legacy `audit` table does not yet exist the DDL-only migration aborts, contradicting the "fresh-install (empty audit)" AC and the ensure-based contract.
MAJOR: `audit_ensure_partitions` (the Append 23514 heal) does not take the AUDP advisory lock and never creates months older than `now - horizon`, so a concurrent 42P07 race or a rotated-away past month is not healed — "no event is lost" is not guaranteed; the Go retry also swallows nothing on the second failure.

`audit_hold_after_purge_total` is incremented for the wrong condition (active-hold purge refusal) in `pfaudit-retention`, and the actual spoliation path (`audit_hold_guard` RAISE) emits no metric at all — AC unmet and the alert signal is misleading.

`audit_migration_state` invariant broken: `runPrestage` upserts the copy cursor directly into the projection table, bypassing `audit_migration_state_events`, so the "rebuildable projection of append-only events" property is false.

Every 0014 function is SECURITY DEFINER with `search_path = pg_catalog, public`: any role with CREATE on `public` can shadow functions/types relied upon by these definer-rights paths (classic escalation). `public` must not be in a definer search_path.

`AuditStore.Append` couples the domain data plane to `pgconn`/SQLSTATE details, breaking the datastore-port abstraction, and treats any 23514 as out-of-range — a CHECK-constraint 23514 on `audit` would spuriously route every failing insert into the DDL provisioning path.
`pg_dump` is invoked with the DSN as an argv element (`backup()`), exposing credentials to the process list of any host user; pass via `PGPASSWORD`/`.pgpass` instead.
`PF_AUDIT_FREEZE_BUDGET_SECONDS` only prints a WARNING; the AC says the budget is asserted, so an over-budget freeze passes the gate silently.
Cold archives default to SSE-AES256 (`DefaultSSE`), not the SSE-KMS the AC mandates, and the KMS key id is never required or validated when `PF_AUDIT_SSE=aws:kms`.

`audit_mark_purged` records `purged_at` before object deletion; a mid-purge crash leaves the month refusing restore while objects still exist, with no tool-supported reconciliation path (stranded recoverable data).
`runPrestage` state is written to `audit_migration_state` but no append-only event is recorded for prestage/verify/close progress steps, weakening the audit trail of the migration itself.
MINOR: `RestoreMonth` panics on short month strings (`month[len(month)-6:]`): `validTable` accepts `audit`, so `restore --month audit` crashes rather than erroring.
Restore leaves `audit_restore_YYYYMM` scratch tables in `public` forever — unbounded accumulation, no cleanup or lifecycle story.

Down migration on a post-swap DB runs `DROP SEQUENCE IF EXISTS audit_id_seq` still referenced by live `audit` (2BP01), so `0014.down` cannot even roll back cleanly; the guard should refuse rather than half-apply.

TRUNCATE is only revoked from `PUBLIC`, and ALTER/ATTACH are not explicitly revoked from `pf_app`/`pf_runtime`; the AC's literal "revoked from every role" is unmet (safety currently relies only on ownership).
`runSwap` increments `audit_attach_unhardened_total` when post-swap verification fails — a false positive for the hardening alert.

Several declared metrics (`audit_provision_seconds`, `audit_insert_out_of_range_total`, `audit_drop_total`, `audit_late_insert_total`, `audit_hold_extract_failed_total`) are never emitted anywhere — dashboards wired to them will read zero forever.
No test exercises the restore-rehearsal (`age -d | pg_restore -l`) or the freeze-budget assertion, both AC-required proofs.
NIT: `audit_partition_coverage` declares `v_lead` (lead_months) and never uses it — `lead_months` is dead config despite being part of the coverage contract.
`TableChecksums` comment claims an "order-independent, constant-memory aggregate of row hashes" but the code is an order-dependent streaming hash — misleading documentation.
`audit_provision`'s `TG_TABLE_NAME <> audit_parent()` early return is dead code: the trigger is never cloned onto leaves.
`architect_review.py` raises the diff budget to 400000 chars and `max_tokens` to 16000, materially increasing per-gate cost without a stated cap rationale.
SUMMARY: Solid architectural shape: SQL primitives vs Go orchestration split, catalog-driven resumable swap, enforce-by-privilege hardening, and two-stage retention with holds are the right long-term choices, and the Go/SQL language rule is respected.

Top risks are completeness, not design: the AC-mandated PG16/resume/isolation/non-blocking tests, the EDP startup + cron coverage wiring, and the unlocked `Down` path that can silently strand live audit rows.
Operational integrity gaps (wrong spoliation metric, projection not events-backed, budget only warned, KMS vs AES256, plaintext DSN in argv) need fixing before this is enterprise-grade.
